angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 353,416 km at 37.64 pc = 0.13 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 26.5706 +/- 0.0224 mas (same row, RUWE 1.55): 37.64 pc, no zero-point correction; the RUWE is high, so the astrometry fits a single star poorly, and the parallax is used as published
radiusSource: Radius 0.508 +/- 0.016 solar radii from Kossakowski et al. 2021, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-1201 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2021A&A...656A.124K/abstract): 353,416 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.512 +/- 0.02 solar masses from Kossakowski et al. 2021, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-1201 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2021A&A...656A.124K/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3476 +/- 51 K from Kossakowski et al. 2021, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-1201 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2021A&A...656A.124K/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Kossakowski et al. 2021, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-1201 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2021A&A...656A.124K/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-1201.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.736, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
